title: Advanced Electroencephalography
description: This course builds upon knowledge and skill acquired in basic electroencephalography (EEG) and is an introduction to the abnormal EEG, maturational changes, and the basic electronic principles upon which successful electroencephalographic techniques are based. The course is designed for students enrolled in the Neurodiagnostic Technology program.
outcomes: Students will be able to demonstrate measurement of electrodes sites according to the 10-20 System of Electrode Placement:
Select and record standard montages, annotate wake, drowsy and/or sleep patterns and electrode artifacts, demonstrate and annotate alerting techniques,
Demonstrate patient observation technique, instruct subject on HV and PS procedures, and post recording demonstrate proper cleaning of subject scalp
Identify electrode locations and anatomical correlate. 10-20 system of electrode placement: identify anatomical landmarks,
objectives: Perform and interpret EEG recordings on human volunteers that conform to the Academy of Clinical Neurophysiology Society (ACNS) minimal guidelines.
Perform accurate polysomnography (PSG) patient setup, system & patient calibration, and record a 15 minute baseline study.
Demonstrate electrical safety so as never to risk harm to patient or self.
List and assess the EEG patterns associated with maturation in the neonatal, term infant, and pediatric (1-16 years) age groups.
List and identify the major abnormal EEG patterns.
Compare and contrast basic electronic terminology and correctly calculate voltage, current, and resistance in parallel and series circuits.
Describe and utilize all of the operational components of the EEG instrument and utilize basic troubleshooting techniques.
List and define the common uses and EEG effects from the major drugs seen as an EEG technologist.
List the major historical contributions made to the scientific field of neurodiagnostics.
content: Common mode rejection ratio and input impedance
Safety procedures inside the clinical EEG laboratory
Safety procedures outside the clinical EEG laboratory
Abnormal EEG patterns and their significance
EEG recording in suspected cerebral death
EEG effects from commonly prescribed medications
Indications, contraindications, side effects, and uses of common drugs
Each week in the classroom lab, students will perform accurate and interpretable EEG recordings on human volunteers using the Academy of Clinical Neurophysiology Society (ACNS) minimal guidelines.
assignments: Professional journal articles including Journal of Clinical Neurophysiology and Neurodiagnostic Journal
Completing four EEG's including one collodion application and one accurate PSG set-up and system-patient calibration.
Identifying the common uses and EEG effects from the major drugs seen as an EEG technologist.
